method: Composite of fundamentals (25%), valuation (20%), technicals (20%), catalyst (20%) and smart money (15%). Technicals and, where a reverse-DCF applies, valuation are computed from the Fri 2026-09-25 close; the rest are analyst judgement.

names.note: Record $60.9bn of AI orders and a $95bn backlog, and the stock just reclaimed +5% on Friday after pulling back from a 595.51 high. It is flat over two weeks, which means the fundamentals have caught up to the price.

Muse is the first consumer AI agent to beat ChatGPT on the App Store, and it moved the whole chip complex on Sep 21. Five brokers raised targets; the stock is up 16% in two weeks and sits 3.6% under its high.
Enterprise AI is standardising on Microsoft: Copilot passed 30 million paid seats, Azure is growing 43%, and Friday's +3.66% came with two target raises in three days.

Earnings in three sessions with the highest expected growth rate in its history. The stock has already rebounded ~17% into the print, so the set-up is about the gross-margin guide, not the headline beat.
The market's new AI-compute co-leader: a $1T valuation reached on Sep 21 on the Meta Muse-driven chip rally, and a record close of 630.63 on Friday, 1.3% under its 639 intraday high.
A defensive leader in the one non-tech group making highs: the post-Humira transition worked, and the stock is within 2% of its peak. Added to the book this week.
The toll-road on AI silicon: whichever designer wins (NVDA, AMD, custom ASICs) the wafers come from TSMC. Up 4% in two weeks and 5.9% off the high with the chip complex at records.
The quality way to own AI networking: near its high, holding gains through the Sep 16 hike and the yield spike, and less crowded than the server names.
The value way into AI servers: a raised FY26 guide on 34-37% revenue growth, trading near its high at a far lower multiple than Dell. Added to the book this week.
A US-China agreement that shelters US agricultural exports is a direct demand signal for farm equipment, and Deere is already near its high.
The Fed did hike, and a positively sloped curve (10y 5.17% vs 2y 4.81%) is good for NII — yet JPM slipped 3.7% as money chased tech. Q3 earnings in mid-October are the catalyst.
The cyber leader in an AI-threat spending cycle: up ~38% in a month to new highs, then a healthy -2.9% Friday as Bernstein warned the group had 'gotten over its skis'. Added to the book this week.
The equipment layer of AI power is working even as utilities de-rate: ETN is up 3.4% in two weeks while CEG and VST fell ~7%. Own the picks and shovels, not the generators.

worst.note: A quality compounder de-rated 30% as rates rose and AI agents threatened seat-based software. Cheap relative to its own history, but the catalyst is missing.
Liquid cooling is mandatory for GB300-class racks, yet VRT is still a third below its high. Friday's +3.25% was the first sign of life; it needs follow-through.
Management pre-announced a softer Q3 trading quarter and higher costs, and the stock fell 9.1% in two weeks. It is 18.9% off its high — cheaper, but the estimate cuts may not be done.
The clearest laggard in AI silicon: 28.7% off its high while merchant GPU names hit records. The custom-ASIC business is intact, so the question is when money rotates back.

The AI-power narrative has broken down on the tape: 36% off the high, and the worst sector this week alongside energy as long yields climbed. The assets are fine; the multiple is being re-priced to a 5% risk-free rate.
4% from its 52-week low with utilities the second-worst sector of the week. The reason to hold it (AI power scarcity) is not being paid for.
